questions.text: What is the shell register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: Offsets as in registers.map: 0x00 DESIGN_ID, 0x04 BYTE_IN, 0x08 TICK, 0x0C REPLY_LEN, 0x10 REPLY_WORD_SEL, 0x14 REPLY_WORD, 0x18 TELEM_LEN, 0x1C TELEM_WORD_SEL, 0x20 TELEM_WORD, 0x24 TAKE, 0x28 STATUS; all 32-bit.
questions.reason: The request names these shell registers but gives no offsets.
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)

questions.text: What happens if the take register is written with no frame held, or a tick write arrives while earlier ticks are pending?

questions.answer: Take with no frame is ignored; a new tick write replaces the remaining pending count.

questions.text: What is the maximum packet size the block must buffer, and what happens beyond it?
questions.default: Buffer 16 bytes (4 header + 8 payload + 4 CRC); any longer packet is counted too long.
questions.reason: A packet can never validly exceed 16 bytes.
questions.answer: Buffer 16 bytes (4 header + 8 payload + 4 CRC); any longer packet is counted too long.

questions.text: Is the telemetry frame count the number of frames held since reset?
questions.default: Yes, frames held since reset, wrapping at 65536.
questions.reason: The request states it only loosely.
questions.answer: Partly. The specification says the frame count changes only when a frame is held and is cleared only by reset, which supports counting frames held since reset. It does not state the wrap-at-65536 behaviour explicitly; the only related text is that the count is 16 bit wide. The wrap part is not specified.
questions.evidence: Frame sequence and frame count change only when a frame is held and only reset clears them.
